comparison.objective: Unlock, orient, and reclamp an angle-grinder guard toward an operator marker; candidate precisely adjusts and jam-nut-locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then cycles it.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1825 tests stabilizing a loose tool, opening an over-center lever, rotating a large guard, reclamping it, and avoiding the disc; candidate tests two-tool coaxial seating, coupled screw/nut countertorque, setting preservation, regrasping, and functional actuation.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1825 requires the guard within 30° of the operator, lever shut, grinder pose preserved, safe clearance, and two-second dwell; candidate requires a 90° stop within 3°, at most 2° drift over three cycles, both nuts retained, and one-second tool clearance.
comparison.reason: This is the closest record because both adjust an angle, lock it, and release, but lever-unlock/guard-orientation tests coarse safety positioning while the candidate tests precision concentric screw-and-jam-nut countertorque plus cyclic retention; all guard-angle, clamp, damage, clearance, and dwell rubric details are present.
